selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What Qur’anic teaching is placed at the beginning of this passage?
questions.answer: It says that the prescribed prayers have fixed times for believers.

questions.question: What complaint did the elderly man make about the prayers?
questions.answer: He said praying five times every day feels too much and becomes tiring because it keeps continuing.

questions.question: When the speaker later examined himself, what did he hear from his lower self?
questions.answer: He heard the same objection that the man had voiced earlier.

questions.question: How did the speaker interpret those words after reflecting on them?
questions.answer: He understood them as coming from a soul inclined to wrong and influenced by Satan.

questions.question: Why did the speaker decide to begin with himself rather than with other people?
questions.answer: He believed a person who has not corrected his own lower self is not ready to correct others.

questions.question: How many warnings does the speaker say he will give to his lower self?
questions.answer: Five.

questions.question: What spiritual condition of the lower self is described before those warnings are given?
questions.answer: It is shown as ignorant, lazy, idle, and heedless.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the source of spiritual excuses against worship?
questions.answer: It suggests such excuses may feel personal, but they are tied to inner weakness and satanic prompting.

questions.question: How is this section introduced structurally in the passage?
questions.answer: It is introduced as the first station of a larger section called the Twenty-First Word.

questions.question: What religious phrase appears before the main discussion begins?
questions.answer: The opening begins with mentioning Allah’s name and His mercy and compassion.

questions.question: What kind of person first raised the objection about prayer?
questions.answer: It was a person described as advanced in age, physically impressive, and socially important.

questions.question: What exactly bothered that person about the prayer schedule?
questions.answer: He felt the repeated daily pattern of five prayers was excessive and wearisome.

questions.question: What happened a long time after that conversation?
questions.answer: The speaker listened inwardly and found the same complaint rising from his own lower self.

questions.question: What role does laziness play in the speaker’s understanding of the lower self?
questions.answer: Laziness is described as the channel through which harmful suggestions were being received.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the lower self commanding evil mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means the lower self naturally pushes a person toward wrong unless it is trained and corrected.

questions.question: How is the lower self addressed at the end of the target passage?
questions.answer: It is called to listen to five warnings that answer its mistaken and lazy objections.

questions.question: What obligation is emphasized through the Qur’anic verse in this passage?
questions.answer: The duty of performing the prescribed prayers at their appointed times.

questions.question: What human feeling toward worship is brought up through the old man’s statement?
questions.answer: A feeling of tiredness and frustration with repeated religious duties.

questions.question: Why is the old man’s statement important to the rest of the passage?
questions.answer: It becomes the starting point for a deeper reflection on the same weakness inside the speaker himself.

questions.question: What does the speaker discover by listening carefully to his inner self?
questions.answer: He discovers that his own lower self is repeating the same complaint against prayer.

questions.question: According to the passage, is this complaint treated as harmless personal preference or as a moral-spiritual danger?
questions.answer: It is treated as a moral-spiritual danger connected to evil influence.

questions.question: How does the speaker move from diagnosis to action?
questions.answer: He admits his own need for reform and decides to address his lower self directly.

questions.question: What principle about leadership or guidance appears in the speaker’s self-criticism?
questions.answer: A person should first work on his own inner state before trying to improve others.

questions.question: How is the lower self portrayed in the final sentence of the target passage?
questions.answer: It is portrayed as speaking from deep ignorance, laziness, and spiritual heedlessness.
